02 / Our home bases

Five stays, fourteen nights.

Three nights in Kyoto and Takayama, two nights in a Nagano ryokan, one night in a Shibu Onsen ryokan, and five nights in Tokyo. No one-night stop except the onsen experience.

Ryokan strategy

Three nights of Japanese hospitality.

In Nagano, Uruoikan is our leading candidate: natural hot springs and a gorge-view bath, with a shuttle to Nagano Station. In Shibu Onsen, choose a traditional ryokan in the village with dinner and breakfast and access to the nine public baths.

Accommodation choices and room availability are not confirmed. Ask about four-person rooms, meal times and luggage forwarding. See hotel options and prices ↓

03 / Where to sleep

Where we sleep, in tiers.

Everyone gets a private room: either a whole home with 3 bedrooms (Airbnb or Booking) or 3 rooms in a hotel or ryokan (a double for the couple, 2 singles). Ryokans in Nagano and Shibu, best neighbourhoods everywhere, and we favoured places with lots of reviews. Live prices for our dates, checked 20 Nov 2026. Tokyo is covered by the conference Hilton. Open a stop, read where to stay and what's typical, then book or add it to the budget.

04 / A travel guide to our stops

Temples, mountains & hot springs.

The character of the trip changes with each chapter — from the old capital to the alpine towns, then the metropolis. Photographs show the locations; winter weather and snow are not guaranteed.

28 Nov – 1 Dec · 3 nights

Kyoto
京都

Start in the former imperial capital, where temples, narrow lanes and autumn foliage set the tone for the trip. Two full days allow us to explore the eastern historic districts and Arashiyama without squeezing in another city.

  • Higashiyama & Gion: Kiyomizu-dera, preserved streets, Yasaka Shrine, evening wander.
  • Arashiyama: bamboo grove, river, gardens and temples.
  • Optional: Fushimi Inari if time permits.
1–3 Dec · 2 nights

Nagano
長野

A convenient base between mountain villages, with time for Zenko-ji's atmospheric temple grounds and a day out to Matsumoto. Return each evening to our ryokan rather than moving between hotels.

  • Zenko-ji: historic Buddhist temple, Nakamise shopping street.
  • Matsumoto: black castle, moats and old town; an easy 50-minute train ride.
  • Relax: a natural onsen if we choose Uruoikan.
Ryokan candidate ↗
3 Dec · 1 night

Snow monkeys & Shibu Onsen
渋温泉

Meet the Japanese macaques at Jigokudani, then step into the traditional hot spring village for our most special overnight. The nine historic communal baths are part of the experience when staying in the village.

  • Morning: bus from Nagano and the forest trail to the park.
  • Afternoon: Shibu Onsen, check-in, yukata and onsen hopping.
  • Evening: traditional ryokan dinner. Optional Obuse only if the day allows.
Friend's exit: after the monkeys, return to Nagano and take the Hokuriku Shinkansen to Tokyo. The rest of us can continue to Shibu Onsen.
4–7 Dec · 3 nights

Takayama
高山

In the mountains of Gifu, Takayama has beautifully preserved wooden merchant houses, a lively food scene and a small-town atmosphere. The third night lets us take a full day trip to Shirakawa-go without any luggage.

  • Sanmachi Suji: Edo-era wooden streets and family-run shops.
  • Morning markets: local produce, crafts and snacks.
  • Food: Hida beef, sake breweries and miso-based dishes.
  • Optional: Takayama Jinya or Hida Folk Village if time allows.
Takayama tourism ↗
6 Dec · Day trip

Shirakawa-go
白川郷

The UNESCO-listed mountain village is the excursion we are keeping. Its steep gassho-zukuri thatched roofs are designed to withstand heavy snowfall. Explore the lanes, visit a farmhouse and head to the Ogimachi viewpoint if open.

  • Transport: direct Nohi Bus from Takayama, about 50 minutes each way.
  • Plan: arrive in the morning and spend 3–5 hours.
  • Return: same Takayama hotel; no luggage during the day.
Bus timetable & reservations ↗
7–12 Dec · 5 nights

Tokyo
東京

Return to Tokyo one day before the conference, then use evenings and any free time for food, neighbourhoods, shopping and the city's nightlife.

  • 7 Dec: arrive and settle in before the conference.
  • 8–11 Dec: conference; optional evenings in Shibuya, Shinjuku, Asakusa or Ginza.
  • 12 Dec: airport and departure.

Friend's early exit

3 December · Nagano to Tokyo.

The easiest split is after the monkey park. Your friend takes a bus back to Nagano Station and boards the direct Hokuriku Shinkansen to Tokyo (~1 h 20–50 min on the train). Everyone else proceeds to Shibu for the ryokan.

Leaving from Takayama later is possible but takes roughly 4–4.5 hours via Nagoya or Toyama. If the friend travels onward with the group, check accommodation occupancy accordingly.

Travel tips

Make transfers predictable.

  • Reserve Shinkansen and limited-express seats for the group, especially the Hida Express.
  • Use a digital IC card or physical Suica/PASMO for compatible local services; check rural bus fare methods.
  • Book Shirakawa-go buses both ways, using the revised 1 December timetable.
  • Keep the airport transfer flexible if flights or immigration are delayed.

08 / Practical details

Less luggage, more Japan.

Suitcases

One forwarding step.

Carry suitcases Kyoto → Nagano. Ask the Nagano ryokan to forward the large bags to Takayama, preferably 1–2 days ahead with the hotel accepting them. Carry a backpack to the monkeys and the Shibu overnight.

Keep two days of clothes, medication, valuables and travel documents with you. If sending bags is not feasible, check with the ryokan about luggage storage before visiting the park.

Car rental

Not necessary.

Train to Matsumoto; bus to the monkeys; local taxi or bus for Shibu; Hida train to Takayama. A four-person taxi for short connections is sensible if buses are awkward.

Renting a car would add a return obligation after the Shibu overnight and winter-driving risk in the mountains.

Late autumn

Dress for layers.

Kyoto may still have colourful leaves; temperatures in the Alps can drop sharply at night. Snow is possible, not guaranteed.

  • Warm layer, gloves, hat, waterproof outer layer.
  • Shoes with good grip for the monkey park.
  • Small daypack; keep luggage out of the rural excursions.
What we deliberately cut: Nakasendo hike (Magome/Tsumago), Nara, Kanazawa, Hakone, Kawaguchiko and the Matsumoto overnight. DisneySea and shopping do not have dedicated days; Tokyo sightseeing is flexible around the conference. We keep Shirakawa-go and the Shibu Onsen ryokan.
